title: Sequencing Fence and Slot Coordination Manual
author: Priya Ramanathan
content:
Summary:
This manual describes the sequencing fence and slot coordination model used by the execution coordinator and kernel scheduler to preserve SLOs under mixed workloads. It combines the admission (rate-fence) model, slot reservation semantics, and reactive backpressure with practical tuning steps, diagnostics, and a short benchmarking protocol for validating changes.

Scope and goals:
- Define semantics: what a sequencing fence is, how slots are reserved/released, and guarantees provided to callers.
- Provide configuration table of key knobs with safe default ranges.
- Give step-by-step tuning recipes for common workload classes (conversational, batch embeddings, long-completion document generation).
- Runbook for operational incidents involving slot exhaustion, priority inversion, and noisy-tenant interference.
- Benchmark and profiling procedure to validate changes to marshaling and coordination paths.

Audience:
- Runtime engineers (primary), SREs oncall, platform PMs, and solutions engineers who operate Dedicated/Private deployments.

Background and motivation:
Redwood's serving runtime multiplexes heterogeneous requests across a pool of kernels. Without coordinated sequencing and slot fencing, high-concurrency short requests can starve long-running kernels (priority inversion) or fragment GPU resources causing KV-cache churn. The sequencing fence enforces a deterministic execution order for critical request classes and exposes quota/slot accounting so higher layers can make routing/fallback decisions.

Concepts and definitions:
1) Slot: an opaque capacity unit representing a kernel execution entitlement (not a single GPU thread). Slots have attributes: affinity (GPU type), duration_hint (ms), priority, and cohort_id (cohort for routing).
2) Sequencing fence: a lightweight barrier injected by the execution coordinator that serializes the order of token-emit critical sections across slots in a shard. Fences are soft (preemption allowed) or hard (no preemption while holding).
3) Rate-fence (admission): policy layer that rejects/queues requests based on token cost projection and current active_slots. It is evaluated pre-scheduling and periodically recomputed from telemetry.
4) Reservation lease: ephemeral lease recorded in slot ledger; auto-renewed by the kernel operator or released on heartbeat loss.

Architecture (text diagram):
- Frontend API -> admission layer (rate-fence) -> execution coordinator -> slot ledger -> scheduler -> kernel dispatcher -> GPU kernels
- Observability hooks: admission.decisions, slot.ledger.delta, fence.events, kernel.handoff.trace

Key metrics and SLO guardrails:
- slot_utilization_pct (SLO: >= 60% and <= 90% under steady state)
- fence_hold_time_p50/p95 (target < 3ms / < 25ms for soft fences)
- admission_reject_rate (target < 1% for premium tenants; overall < 5%)
- priority_inversion_incidents (count; alarm if > 0 over 15m for dedicated clusters)

Configuration table (knobs and safe defaults):
- admission.window_seconds: 1 - 60 (default 5) — sliding window used to project token cost.
- slot.max_concurrent_per_gpu: 8 - 256 (default 64) — soft cap, tuned per-GPU family.
- fence.type: soft | hard | hybrid (default hybrid) — hybrid uses soft by default, switches to hard for long duration ops.
- reservation.lease_ms: 2000 - 30000 (default 8000)
- priority.boost_threshold_ms: 50 - 200 (default 100) — if a request waits longer than this, it receives temporary priority boost.

Tuning recipes (high-level):
1) Conversational (many short requests, strict p95 latency):
   - Reduce admission.window_seconds to 2s.
   - Enable fence.hybrid with soft locked for inference emission.
   - Lower slot.max_concurrent_per_gpu for the cohort serving chat to 32 to reduce kernel contention.
   - Observe fence_hold_time_p95; if > 20ms, increase per-cohort isolation (dedicated slots).

2) Embeddings batch (large batch throughput):
   - Increase admission.window_seconds to 10s to allow batching.
   - Set reservation.lease_ms to 12000 to reduce churn.
   - Use hard fences for batch completion steps to ensure KV-cache coherency.

3) Long-document generation (high duration, medium concurrency):
   - Use hybrid fences that escalate to hard when duration_hint > 2000ms.
   - Pre-reserve slots at admission time (reservation.preallocate=true).
   - Enable priority_boost_threshold_ms for tail mitigation.

Operational runbook: Slot exhaustion incident
1) Detection: alert if slot_utilization_pct > 95% OR admission_reject_rate > 10% sustained for 5m.
2) Immediate mitigation actions (oncall):
   - Identify noisy cohort: query slot.ledger.delta for top 5 cohort_id by delta_slots over last 5m.
   - If noisy tenant is non-critical, apply temporary quota reduction: curl -XPOST $COORDINATOR/admin/quota -d '{"cohort_id":"X","max_slots":N}'
   - If widespread, enable emergency shedding: admission.mode=reject-nonpremium
3) Root-cause steps:
   - Pull kernel traces: use ingest tool: ./tools/collect-trace --trace-type kernel-handoff --since 15m > /tmp/handoff.trace
   - Inspect fence.events for hard fence hold durations: query metrics.fence_hold_time_p95
   - Check slot lease churn: count heartbeat timeouts in slot.ledger events.
4) Post-incident: run traffic-simulation to reproduce the spike and iterate tuning (see Benchmarking section).

Priority inversion detection & mitigation
- Detection signal: priority_inversion_incidents > 0 OR slow_p99 among high-priority cohort increases > 3x baseline.
- Fast mitigation: enable short preemption window (fence.preempt_window_ms = 25) and run a micro-eviction for low-priority ephemeral slots.
- Longer remediation: adjust scheduler.policy_weights to favor latency-sensitive cohorts and schedule gradual capacity increase for that cohort.

Diagnostics and observability guidance:
- Traces to collect: admission.decisions, slot.ledger.snap, fence.events, kernel.handoff.trace. Collect correlated traces for a single request id (request_id in logs).
- Dashboards: "Slot Ledger Health" (shows active slots by cohort, lease churn, heartbeat failures) and "Fence Latency" (p50/p95 across shard regions).
- Useful log queries (example):
  - Find requests that waited > 200ms in admission:
    kubectl logs -l app=coordinator | jq -r 'select(.admission_wait_ms>200) | .request_id, .cohort'

Benchmarking & profiling protocol (short):
1) Goal: validate scheduler change does not regress p95 for conversational and does improve throughput for batching.
2) Setup: shadow cluster with identical kernel profiles; use synthetic traffic generator (tools/traffic-gen) with two profiles: conversational (10–200 tokens, 100–600 rps) and batch_embeddings (batch_size 256–1024, 5–20 feeds/s).
3) Measurements: p50/p95/p99 latency, admission_reject_rate, slot_utilization_pct, fence_hold_time_p95.
4) Pass criteria: conversational p95 <= baseline * 1.05 and batch throughput >= baseline + 8% with comparable slot_utilization.
5) Profiling tips: capture kernel-level nvprof traces for a sample of > 100 high-latency events and use trace-annotator to correlate with fence.events.

Safe rollout checklist for config changes:
1) Feature flag behind runtime-sandbox and canary cohort.
2) Unit-level canary: enable on single shard and run 30m synthetic load.
3) Canary-level: enable on 10% of shards; run 2h with auto-rollback threshold set (conversational_p95_increase>3%).
4) Full rollout: staged 25% increments with 30m observation windows.

Sample config snippets (YAML):
---
admission:
  window_seconds: 5
  mode: adaptive
slot:
  max_concurrent_per_gpu: 64
  reservation:
    lease_ms: 8000
fence:
  type: hybrid
  preempt_window_ms: 25
  priority_boost_threshold_ms: 100
---

CLI utilities (examples):
- Reserve slots for cohort: rslot reserve --cohort chat-pt1 --slots 20 --duration-ms 600000
- Dump ledger snapshot: rslot dump --shard shard-3 --out /tmp/ledger.snap
- Apply quota: curl -XPOST $COORD_ADMIN/quota --data '{"cohort_id":"chat-pt1","max_slots":20}'

Troubleshooting checklist (when p95 regresses):
- Are fence_hold_time_p95 or p99 elevated? If yes, inspect kernel.handoff.trace for hot kernels.
- Is slot_utilization saturated? If > 95%, consider throttling noncritical cohorts.
- Check for heartbeat/lease thrashing (slot.ledger.heartbeat_failures). If present, increase reservation.lease_ms temporarily.
- Validate admission.window_seconds; too-short windows can cause over-eager rejection, too-long windows delay batching opportunities.

Security and safety considerations:
- Reservation ledger writes are audited; changes to quota must be performed through admin APIs (audit.log entries created).
- Do not set reservation.lease_ms > 60s in multi-tenant clusters — leads to allocation hoarding under failure.

Appendix A — Change validation checklist for scheduler kernel rollouts:
- Confirm kernel ABI compatibility via kernel-compat-matrix.
- Run end-to-end shadowing with live traffic sampling (1% of traffic) for 24h.
- Verify no increase in priority_inversion_incidents and no >5% increase in admission_reject_rate.

Appendix B — Contact and ownership:
- Primary owner: Priya Ramanathan (serving-runtime team)
- Oncall escalation: eng-sre oncall -> public slack #runtime-oncall -> PagerDuty (runtime-sre)
- Feedback loop: open an ADR or a runtime-team RFC and link the simulation results.
